children: Sonic’s actual supply of its native S token has been found to be about 48% higher than originally disclosed.
Wu Blockchain reported on November 20 that Sonic said an independent audit showed the token’s total supply was about 4.7 billion, rather than the previously announced 3.175 billion.
The supply discrepancy was linked to a past token issuance process on the Fantom network, Sonic’s predecessor.

The audit found that when about 2.12 billion native FTM tokens were issued on the Fantom Opera network in 2019, roughly 1.47 billion corresponding Ethereum-based ERC-20 FTM tokens were left neither locked nor burned.

When the same asset is transferred across different networks, the original tokens are typically locked or burned to prevent duplicate supply. Sonic said some ERC-20 FTM tokens were not handled that way at the time, resulting in the mismatch.

Sonic said the issue was the main reason the actual supply of the S token far exceeded its previously announced figure. The project is still investigating the specific circumstances behind the discrepancy during the earlier issuance process.
Sonic also announced follow-up measures to strengthen supply controls. It plans to remove the ability to issue tokens manually to block any future discretionary issuance.

The project also plans to burn 91.7 million unallocated S tokens on December 15. But that burn is smaller than the gap between the previously reported and actual supply figures, leaving attention on the outcome of the additional probe into past issuance and any further response.

title: Sonic Says Actual S Token Supply Is 48% Higher Than Previously Reported After Issuance Error
